title: Kruskal's output preserves connectivity
statement: Fix $n \in \bbn$, and let $E$ be a list of weighted edges on the vertex set $\mathrm{Fin}\,n$. Then the edge list $\mathrm{kruskal}\,n\,E$ produced by Kruskal's algorithm on $E$ spans $E$: for every pair of vertices $u, v \in \mathrm{Fin}\,n$, if $u$ and $v$ are connected by a path through the edges of $E$, then they are also connected by a path through the selected edges $\mathrm{kruskal}\,n\,E$.
hypotheses_covered: E is a list of weighted edges on Fin n
replaced:
For every weighted edge list $E$ over $\mathrm{Fin}\,n$, the output $\mathrm{kruskal}\,n\,E$
spans like $E$: any two vertices reachable in $E$ are reachable using only the selected
edges.
